title: Wildfire Season: The Continuity Checklist | Pro Link Systems
caption:
Most Southern California businesses have a continuity plan.

Very few have ever run it.

Those are not the same thing, and the gap between them shows up on exactly one kind of day — the one where a public safety power shutoff arrives on schedule, announced days in advance, and completely outside your control.

What decides how that day goes isn't the size of the binder. It's whether anyone has opened it.

We made a 90-second film about the three things we check, in the order we check them:

1. Sequence. Not everything has to come back at once — but something has to come back first. Decide that before you need it, not at 7am in a dark office.

2. Location. A copy of what matters, somewhere the same outage can't reach.

3. Rehearsal. Run it on an ordinary Tuesday, when nothing is wrong.

The third one is the one everyone skips. It's also the only one that makes the first two real.

We've been doing this in Los Angeles since 1999. The checklist we use is free — link in the first comment.

Every October, the wind picks up and somebody in the office asks whether we're covered if the power goes out.

The honest answer for most Southern California businesses is: there's a plan, and nobody has ever run it.

A public safety power shutoff isn't an emergency — it's scheduled, announced, and completely out of your hands. What decides how the day goes is whether anyone has actually tested the plan on a normal day, when nothing was wrong.

We made a short film about the three things we check: what comes back first, where the copy lives, and whether anyone has rehearsed it.

We've been doing this from Woodland Hills since 1999. The checklist we use is free — no form, no pitch:

THE THREE MOVES
1. Sequence — not everything has to come back at once, but something has to come back first. Decide the order before you need it.
2. Location — keep a copy of what matters somewhere the same outage can't reach.
3. Rehearsal — run it on an ordinary Tuesday, when nothing is wrong. This is the step almost everyone skips, and it's the one that makes the other two real.
